newsitem.title: UK: Dlr grinds higher in Europe as stg extends gains.
newsitem.headline: Dlr grinds higher in Europe as stg extends gains.

text.p: The dollar ground higher against the mark at the European midsession, boosted mainly by sterling/mark's push to over six-year highs, said dealers.
Sterling/mark pushed above 2.98, testing its highest levels since April 1991, fuelled by ongoing expectations of further UK rate rises after Thursday's quarter-point hike.
This helped dollar/mark regain territory above 1.76 marks and levels it held before Thursday's retreat on the mark positive comments from Bundesbank President Hans Tietmeyer.
"The dollar's climb today is really all down to sterling/mark," said a U.S. bank analyst.

The impact of Tietmeyer's remarks Thursday, in which he wanted to see a strong mark going into euro and that the dollar's correction against the mark was over, had waned by morning Europe with the mark giving up most of yesterday's across-the-board gains.

"Tietmeyer's remarks gave the mark boost but that has now faded," said Sonja Gibbs, market strategist at Nomura International. "Focus is on the contents of the German budget but this is unlikely to change the perception of a broad EMU."
The German cabinet said today it approved the 1998 draft and 1997 supplementary budgets.
The extra budget for 1997 raises the projected deficit to 71.2 bln marks from an original plan of 53.3 bln but the government has said it still expects to qualify for EMU.
German Finance Minister Theo Waigel is holding a news conference at 1200 GMT to present details of today's budget Cabinet meeting.
Dollar/mark stood at 1.7610/15 at 1110 GMT compared with 1.7505/10 late Thursday in Europe.
Mark/yen, meantime, retreated from its early session highs around 65.00 yen back to the key resistance point of 64.60 yen it broke on Thursday.
U.S. June producer price data is due at 1230 GMT with an average of analysts' forecasts pointing to no change in the core month-on-month data and only a 0.1 percent increase year/year.
"The data should help underline the subdued outlook of pipeline inflation in the U.S.," said Jeremy Hawkins, chief economist at Bank of America.
Today's figures are unlikely to raise expectations of a U.S. rate rise in the near-term, he said.
Dollar/yen was firmer but still fighting shy of resistance at 114.00. At 1130 GMT, dollar/yen stood at 133.80/85 against 113.03/13 yen late Thursday.
Dealers said comments overnight from a former senior Japanese Ministry of Finance official that U.S. and Japan authorities could step in if the dollar/yen goes below 110 yen lent dollar/yen support.
"This was certainly a factor overnight but this confirms the market perception of a 110 yen bottom," said a Japanese bank dealer.
